Featured Project – Final Year Project

Individual project work and details

Status: FYP-I proposal stage · analysis and results in progress

BIM and Life Cycle Assessment of a Green and Thermally Efficient Residential Building

This project focuses on designing and modeling a sustainable and thermally efficient residential bungalow using Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), considering Sukkur’s hot climatic conditions.

Project Features

  • G+1 residential bungalow design (RCC structure), 100 Ft Road, Sukkur.
  • Autodesk Revit BIM and 3D building model.
  • Life Cycle Assessment of building materials.
  • Environmental impact assessment.
  • Thermal efficiency and heat gain reduction.
  • Green and sustainable materials: hollow bricks, 30% GGBS concrete, triple-glazed windows, recycled paper-fibre insulation.

Software & Aim

Autodesk RevitOne Click LCA

Aim: to compare the thermal performance and life-cycle environmental impact of a green bungalow with a conventional residential building using BIM and LCA.

Key Projects & Research

Final-year level design and published research

Low-Cost Sustainable Multi-Story Commercial Plaza (2026)

  • G+3 commercial plaza on a 30m × 40m site in Sukkur, beam-slab system.
  • Structural analysis and design in ETABS v20 for dead, live, wind and seismic loads.
  • Full BIM model in Revit and detailed drawings in AutoCAD.
  • 30% fly ash concrete, hollow bricks and thermal optimization.
  • 12–15% cost reduction while meeting IS 456, IS 875 and IS 1893.

Beam-slab system, ETABS v20 loads: dead, live, wind and seismic. Sustainable features targeted lower cost and a thermally optimized design.

Research: Wood Saw Dust as Partial Fine Aggregate in Concrete

  • Research article published on LinkedIn (March 2026).
  • Studied strength, durability and sustainability of concrete using waste material.
  • Lab work on beam behavior under loading, hydrograph analysis and material testing.

Published as a research article on LinkedIn in March 2026 on waste-material use in concrete.
